Great job in the Kentucky House on “the chicken bill!” This bill would finally allow Kentucky farmers and shoppers to take full advantage of the federal exemption for small farms/processors. Buy local, eat healthy.


Savannah Maddox (@SavannahLMaddox)

I am pleased to report that the language of a bill I have filed every year since 2021 (along with Rep. Josh Bray), has passed in the House. It is colloquially known as “the chicken bill!”

Today I met with seniors from @AugustaSchools during their trip to the Capitol.

I took them to the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee room where I serve, so they could get a feel for what it's like to participate in a hearing!

Thanks to the students for visiting.

If the shoe doesn’t fit…

Yesterday I visited Peach Blossom Farm in Waddy, Kentucky, where Matthew and Leslie Corcione raise Wagyu-Angus cattle.

Doc Carlen Pippin of Veterans Rural Outreach and Todd Murphy of @USACares joined us. We discussed the work they're doing to improve the lives of KY veterans.
Bonus: meme mentioned in the article!😂

I’ll continue to support the valid Constitutional position that Trump, Jordan, and Vance have all expressed strongly in the past:

No FISA reauthorization without a warrant requirement for US citizens!

If I lose, nobody’s going to stick their head up. The entire GOP will be a rubber stamp. If I win, there’ll be more people like @FmrRepMTG, @RepBoebert, & @RepNancyMace who are willing to go against the grain when it’s unambiguously the right thing to do.

Thank you Paul & Daisy Hamilton & family for hosting us at your restaurant. It was great to see so many, including State Senator @AaronReed4KY; Shelby County J/E Dan Ison & Deputy J/E Jon Park; Sheriff Mark Moore; Simpsonville Admin Steve Eden; & County Jailer Sandra Ashcraft.

.@SenRandPaul & I joined over 30 local officials, public servants, and business owners/execs, for a round table discussion at The Farm Kitchen in Shelbyville, KY, yesterday.

We got to engage with constituents, hear their concerns, & learn how we can better serve them in D.C.

The bees were buzzing so loud in the peach orchard this Sunday morning that it was a bit intimidating to stand there! <sound on> Also, one of our ducks laid a double-yoke egg that weighed in at 4.8 ounces, more than double the size of the chicken eggs we bought.

Good morning America! Peach trees are blooming on our farm in Kentucky. I’ve planted about 14 different varieties here over the years.

Thank you, Christine Curran, for emceeing the discussion. Thank you, Shreeukta Adhikari, Christina Gogzheyan, Minerva Shakya, Leah Bishop, and the Nu Rho Psi student members for coordinating the event and inviting me to participate.

Yesterday, I participated in a "Learning to Listen Again" panel discussion hosted by Northern Kentucky University's chapter of @NuRhoPsi, the Neuroscience Honor Society.

The topic was "how to help people advocate more effectively in a politically charged climate."

I'll be hosting Academy Day on Saturday, April 18th. Academy Day allows students and their parents the chance to learn more about attending a U.S. Service Academy.

More information, including a RSVP form, is available on my website.

massie.house.gov/services/us…

I had a great meeting this morning with Etain Connor of @_FEAM. FEAM Aero services planes and employees 146 people at CVG Airport in my district.

One topic we discussed was FAA oversight, which is a central part of my work on the Aviation Subcommittee.
